previous_findings_status.note: All four sites still fetch a fresh installation client and repository handle inside their per-candidate loops: for each CONFIG_FILE_CHAIN path, InstructionsResolver does per fallback path, fetchManifestSection per manifest path, and GitHubIssuesProvider.read per candidate issue — no hoisting was made.

shouldCacheStackAndNotHitApiOnSecondCall still consists of two resolves plus assertEquals(first, second); no verify against the repository mock was restored, so the assertion still passes with or without a cache.
The comment '// The freshly cached entry is served on the next call (System clock is within TTL)' is still directly followed by the closing brace; the second resolve and the verify remain deleted.

The four caching tests still end with resolves and no verify; aReadableButUnusableConfigIsCachedLikeAnyOtherAnswer still carries only the bare '// configured file was the only one read' comment in place of the call-count observation its javadoc claims is tested.
The test still stubs doThrow(new RuntimeException("bad")).when(bad).getContent(); — a read failure, not undecodable content — so it still exercises the READ_FAILED path the name does not describe.

The jakarta.ws.rs.NotFoundException instanceof branch quoted in the finding is gone: fetchAndParse's RuntimeException catch now simply warns and returns READ_FAILED, and the 404 classification moved to its own catch block (though that block is keyed on the wrong exception type — see the new finding).
